statement_record.book: If U : C ⟶ D is faithful, then any diagram in C whose U-image commutes in D already commutes in C: from U f_n ∘ ⋯ ∘ U f_1 = U g_m ∘ ⋯ ∘ U g_1 one concludes f_n ∘ ⋯ ∘ f_1 = g_m ∘ ⋯ ∘ g_1, by functoriality and faithfulness. Consequence: in a concrete category, commutativity of a diagram may be verified elementwise on underlying sets.
statement_record.intree: `fmap_inj {x y} (f g : x ~> y) : fmap[F] f ≈ fmap[F] g → f ≈ g` — the defining field of [Faithful] — together with the functor law `fmap_comp : fmap (f ∘ g) ≈ fmap f ∘ fmap g`. Since the library has no separate type of paths (a composable string IS a morphism), instantiating fmap_inj at the two composites and normalising the hypothesis with fmap_comp is the whole proof.
statement_record.strength_comparison: intree-weaker: only the PARALLEL-PAIR form is asserted, and only as the defining field of the class. dsq_hcomp {a b c a' b' c'} {h : dhor a b} {h' : dhor b c} {u : a ~{dcat}~> a'} {v : b ~{dcat}~> b'} {w : c ~{dcat}~> c'} {k : dhor a' b'} {k' : dhor b' c'} : dsq h u v k → dsq h' v w k' → dsq (dhcomp h' h) u w (dhcomp k' k).

statement_record.book: Commutativity of a pair of adjacent squares implies commutativity of the exterior rectangle, but the converse fails — the 2×3 diagram in Ab with rows Z =id=> Z → 0 and 0 → Z =id=> Z has a commuting outer rectangle though neither square commutes; likewise one square plus the rectangle does not in general give the other. The obstruction: a relation g ∘ h_n ∘ ⋯ ∘ h_1 = g ∘ k_m ∘ ⋯ ∘ k_1 may not be cancelled unless g is left-cancelable (a monomorphism), dually for a common right factor and epimorphisms.
statement_record.intree: The POSITIVE half is in-tree, as the horizontal-pasting field of [DoubleCategory] instantiated at [Sq C], where a square over (h, u, v, k) is literally the proposition `k ∘ u ≈ v ∘ h`: from `k ∘ u ≈ v ∘ h` and `k' ∘ v ≈ w ∘ h'` one gets `(k' ∘ k) ∘ u ≈ w ∘ (h' ∘ h)`. (Vertical pasting, dsq_vcomp, is the transposed reading.) The cancellation vocabulary the remark blames exists as `Monic`/`Epic` (Theory/Morphisms.v:116, :104).
statement_record.strength_comparison: intree-weaker: only the forward pasting is asserted. Nothing negative is stated — no in-tree proposition of the form 'the exterior rectangle commutes while a constituent square does not', and no counterexample category in which to state it.

statement_record.book: Given a --f--> b --j--> c above a' --k--> b' --m--> c' with verticals g, h, l, and supposing the outer rectangle commutes (l ∘ j ∘ f ≈ m ∘ k ∘ g), the data forms a COMMUTATIVE RECTANGLE (both squares commute) if either (i) the right-hand square commutes and m is a monomorphism, or (ii) the left-hand square commutes and f is an epimorphism.
statement_record.intree: Only the underlying cancellation principles are stated, as the defining fields of the two classes: `monic : ∀ z (g1 g2 : z ~> x), f ∘ g1 ≈ f ∘ g2 → g1 ≈ g2` and `epic : ∀ z (g1 g2 : y ~> z), g1 ∘ f ≈ g2 ∘ f → g1 ≈ g2`. statement_record.intree: Neither clause is stated. What is in-tree is the pair of ingredients that yields (ii): terminality is characterised as a limit of the empty diagram in both directions (`Terminal_Limit : Limit F ↔ @Terminal C` for F : 0 ⟶ C), and an equivalence preserves all limits (`equivalence_preserves_limits : PreservesAllLimits F`, obtained from RAPL through the adjoint equivalence). Chaining them — Terminal C ⇒ Limit (0 ⟶ C) ⇒ IsALimit (F ◯ (0 ⟶ C)) ⇒ Limit (0 ⟶ D) ⇒ Terminal D — is a few lines, but is never carried out; the dual route for Initial via colimits (equivalence_preserves_colimits, :432) is likewise available and likewise unused.
